nodes.summary: Resolved true: Keevash, Knox and Mycroft give a polynomial-time algorithm when the minimum codegree is at least `n/k + γn` for a fixed `γ > 0`, and Han extends it to minimum codegree at least `n/k`, so the problem is in `P` for every `1/k ≤ c < 1/2`. Inputs whose edge count is below what the codegree condition forces are rejected first, so `n` is polynomial in the input size whenever the remaining checks run.…
